No, the one from the repository will usually be better than getting it from their site. The mobile line seems to be hit or miss sometimes.
There's three things I know of that you can try depending on your situation:

You could try the new Ubuntu nvidia driver though and see if it helps. Open a terminal and paste this in:

sudo add-apt-repository ppa:graphics-drivers/ppa

That adds the new nvidia driver repo they just started doing.
Then paste this to update the drivers:

sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install nvidia-355

If you're having issues with steam games, you can add Nvidia's threaded optimizations to it by right-clicking on the game in your steam list > properties > set launch options, and pasting this:

__GL_THREADED_OPTIMIZATIONS=1 %command%

One last thing you can do is change the cpu governor if you use your laptop for gaming and have it plugged in most of the time. By default it uses one that tries to preserve more battery at the cost of performance. That makes sense if you're using it for everyday laptop stuff, but not so much if you're using it as a portable gaming system. Paste this in a terminal: 

sudo cpupower frequency-set -g performance

That will set the governor to performance mode rather than the ondemand one it uses by default.
